grading_rubric.A: real modelled leaves/petals (or leaflets), no card planes visible at 5 m, species-recognisable silhouette at 5 m and 15 m, sensible polycount (< ~400k tris)
grading_rubric.B: reads as a plant of this kind at 5 m and 15 m; leaf cards allowed only if no fishbone/flat planes are visible at 5 m; no faceting; usable at garden scale
grading_rubric.C: fails at 5 m (faceted, sparse, flat, wrong scale or wrong foliage) or too small to read at 15 m as a single object
grading_rubric.D: broken, mis-scaled, untextured, a nursery pot on a plane, or not a plant for this garden

rubric_status: POLICY: our own rubric, no published standard; grades are by eye on the preview sheets (5 m and 15 m, 35 mm lens, eye 1.6 m, 4 azimuths) plus the measured stats
drawable_rule: drawable = best asset of the species or its genus has grade A or B; a look-alike species never counts
previews: asset-previews/<id>.jpg (top row camera 5 m, bottom 15 m, azimuth 0/90/180/270; rendered by archpipe.landscape.plants.asset_preview via jobq)

assets.title: Aloe Vera (high)
assets.rationale: Looked at: scanned Aloe rosettes of thick fleshy lanceolate leaves with real marginal spines, 0.3-0.7 m tall and up to 1.1 m across; reads as an aloe at 5 m. A single plant is a dot at 15 m (C alone); a 3 m x 3 m drift of the six variations reads as an aloe bed at 5 m and as a thin dark band at 15 m, so use groups of 10 or more. No flower spike in any variation. Dark but convincing colour.

assets.title: Carolana Water Lily (high)
assets.rationale: Looked at: round floating pads with notched bases and yellow star-shaped flowers on tall stalks and buds; reads as a water-lily patch at 5 m, thin at 15 m. Genus Nymphaea only (asset says 'Nymphaea', a hardy Carolana cultivar): the flower is yellow, not the blue of Nymphaea caerulea/nouchali, and a hardy hybrid says nothing about Cairo heat. Authored with the root plane 0.67 m below the pad plane: set the water line at the pad plane.

assets.title: Grass Lawn (8k)

Use the continuous tiled material (with its displacement as bump), not scattered patches.
